texts.preamble: The Drugs Inspector vs S.Nagireddy And Another on 22 June, 2022 Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender Criminal Appeal No. 94 of 2020 Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. Questioning the acquittal recorded by II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Mancherial (for short 'the Magistrate') in C.C.No.395 of 2016 of the respondents herein for the offence under Section 18a(i) r/w 16(1)(a) punishable under Section 27(d) of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, the present appeal is filed. 2. The Drug Inspector/P.W.1 filed a complaint stating that while he was working as Drug Inspector at Mancherial he inspected Drugs Stores of Area Hospital, Mancherial on 30.04.2013 and picked up sample of drug namely 'Ranitidine 150 mg from the said hospital. The Drug Inspector/P.W.1 followed the procedure prescribed for the sampling and accordingly sent for analysis. At the same time, the Drug Inspector/P.W.1 also collected samples of 'Metronidazole' oral suspension syrup and also sent it for analysis. During the said proceedings, Exs.P1 and P2 were drafted, which are forms 16 and 17, dated 30.04.2013. PW.1 received drug analysis report Ex.P3 stating that the drug 'Ranitidine' was not of standard quality. Accordingly, P.W.1 addressed letter Ex.P5 dated 17.09.2013 to the Medical Superintendent, Government Area Hospital and he received reply vide Ex.P6 informing that the Drug was purchased from M/s.Concord Drugs Limited. Ex.P10 is the letter addressed to the Managing Director of M/s.Concord Drugs Limited and in reply Ex.P11 was issued informing that the said drugs were manufactured by the 2nd respondent/Accused No.2 i.e., M/s.Cortel Laboratories Private Limited. The Drug Inspector/P.W.1 again addressed a letter Ex.P12 to the Managing Director of 1st respondent/A1 and thereafter, the respondents sent reply along with all the details of the drug under Exs.16 to 25. Accordingly, P.W.1, the Drug Inspector found that these respondents had manufactured the said tablet 'Ranitidine' which was not found to be of standard identity, purity and strength in accordance with the Indian Pharma Copoeia, for the said reason, the respondents/accused committed an offence under the Cosmetics and Drugs Act, 1940. 3. Upon appearance, the respondents were examined under Section 251 of Cr.P.C, and the substance of allegation under Section 18(a)(i) r/w 16(1)(a) punishable under Section 27 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, was read over to the accused, they pleaded not guilty. 4. The prosecution examined P.W.1, Drug Inspector, P.W.2 was the pharmacist in the Government Area Hospital, Mancherial where the drugs were seized. 5. During the course of evidence, Exs.P1 to P36 were marked. 6. Learned Magistrate acquitted the respondents on the following grounds; i) P.W.1 is not The Drugs Inspector vs S.Nagireddy And Another on 22 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64947164/ 1 authorized as per Section 22 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act to exercise his powers in Mancherial local limits; ii) The prosecution has not proved that the analysis was done by a government appointed analyst as required under Section 20 of the said Act; iii) any analysis has to be done by a person appointed by the State Government or Central Government; iv) The analysis report has taken several months. However, as per Rule 45 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, a government analyst has to complete analysis within 60 days failing which, such government analyst shall seek extension of time. V) The analysis report Ex.P3 was not served on these respondents and by the time complaint was filed, the drug 'Ranitidine' date expired.
texts.arguments: 7. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that the sole ground on which the present appeal is filed is that the Government analysis report Ex.P3 is clear that the drug supplied by the respondents was found to be not of standard quality, for which reason, the acquittal has to be reversed and accordingly, the respondents be punished for manufacturing and supplying drugs which are not of standard quality. Section 20 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 reads as follows: "20. Government Analysts.-- ( 1) The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint such persons as it thinks fit, having the prescribed qualifications, to be Government Analysts for such areas in the State and in respect of such drugs or 2[classes of drugs or such cosmetics or classes of cosmetics] as may be specified in the notifications. (2) The Central Government may also, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint such persons as it thinks fit, having the prescribed qualifications, to be Government Analysts in respect of such drugs or 2[classes of drugs or such cosmetics or classes of cosmetics] as may be specified in the notification. (3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub- section (2), neither the Central Government nor a State Government shall appoint as a Government Analyst any official not serving under it without the previous consent of the Government under which he is serving.] 3[(4) No person who has any financial interest in the import, manufacture or sale of drugs or cosmetics shall be appointed to be a Government Analyst under sub-section (1) or sub- section (2) of this section.]" 11. In Medipol Pharmaceutical India Private Limited v. Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education & Research and another in Civil Appeal No.2903 of 2020 arising out of SLP (C ) No.26349 of 2019, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: "9) In Laborate Pharmaceuticals India Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu (2018) 15 SCC 93, after referring to Section 25 of the Act, this Court held as follows: "7. The cognizance of the offence(s) alleged in the present case was taken on 4-3-2015 though it appears that the complaint itself was filed on 28-11- 2012. According to the appellant the cough syrup had lost shelf life in the month of November 2012 itself. "11) Likewise, under Section 24 of the Insecticides Act, 1968, this Court in State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid (P) Ltd. (1998) 8 SCC 190 held: "12.
